title: Intervention by a nonparty
summary: Intervention is a procedure by which a person outside the lawsuit seeks to enter it to protect an interest or participate under the rule’s conditions. Rule 24 distinguishes intervention of right from permissive intervention.
notes: The ability to intervene does not automatically impose a duty to intervene on every informed nonparty. The syllabus assigns the chapter but allocates no classroom time to intervention.

sections.Meaning: Intervention is a procedure by which a person outside the lawsuit seeks to enter it to protect an interest or participate under the rule’s conditions. Rule 24 distinguishes intervention of right from permissive intervention.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the applicant’s interest, possible impairment, timeliness, and adequacy of existing representation, or the relevant basis for permissive intervention. Smuck illustrates why a government representative’s broad responsibilities may leave particular interests insufficiently represented.
